rows.question: What dry torque do the capscrews on a size 60 coupling get, in ft-lb?
rows.answer: On the Xylem e-MPA / e-MPR / e-MPD pump, the capscrews on a size 60 coupling are torqued dry to 75 ft-lb (900 in-lb). Do not lubricate the capscrew threads [1].

rows.question: When bumping the motor to check rotation direction, where do I look to see which way it turns?
rows.reference: through the coupling guard or through the motor fan cover
rows.answer: For the Xylem e-MPA / e-MPR / e-MPD pump: first locate the arrows on the adaptor or the motor fan cover to determine the correct rotation direction. Then start the motor and quickly check the direction of rotation through the coupling guard or through the motor fan cover, and stop the motor [1].

rows.question: The pump starts but the residual current device (RCD) trips. What should I check?
rows.reference: Check the insulation of the electrical system components.
rows.answer: The cause is a ground (earth) leakage. Check the insulation of the electrical system components [1].

rows.question: What trip rating should the high-sensitivity differential switch have for protection against lethal shock?
rows.answer: 30 mA. The Xylem e-MPA / e-MPR / e-MPD pump manual says to add additional protection against lethal shock by installing a high-sensitivity differential switch (30 mA) [residual current device RCD] [1].

rows.question: How often do pumps with regreaseable bearings need regreasing?
rows.reference: 4000 operating hours, at least once per year
rows.answer: Regrease at 4000 operating hours, but at least once per year. Clean the lubrication nipples (SN) first and use NLGI Grade 2 grease or equivalent [1].

rows.question: The pump has a star-delta starter and no automatic reset thermal protection. What do I set the thermal relay to?
rows.reference: 58% of the nominal current or operating current
rows.answer: Adjust the thermal relay to 58% of the nominal current or operating current (only for three-phase motors) [1]. That is, 58% of the nominal current value of the electric pump (data plate) if the motor is used with full load, or 58% of the operating current (for example measured with a current pincer) if the motor is used with partial load [1].

rows.question: What grade of grease is specified for regreasing the pump bearings?
rows.answer: For the Xylem e-MPA / e-MPR / e-MPD pump, NLGI Grade 2 grease or equivalent is specified for pumps with regreaseable bearings (regrease at 4000 operating hours, but at least once per year, cleaning the lubrication nipples (SN) first) [1].

rows.question: In the spare parts stock table, what does 'i' stand for?
rows.answer: In the spare parts stock table (Xylem e-MPA / e-MPR / e-MPD), i = number of stages [1].

rows.question: What is the maximum permissible radial misalignment between the coupling halves, in mm?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What command dumps a database in the compressed custom format?
rows.answer:
pg_dump -Fc dbname > filename

This dumps a database using pg_dump's custom dump format, which compresses data as it writes it to the output file if PostgreSQL was built on a system with the zlib compression library installed. A custom-format dump must be restored with pg_restore, e.g. pg_restore -d dbname filename [1].

rows.question: Which pg_dumpall option dumps only the cluster-wide data such as roles and tablespaces?
rows.answer: The pg_dumpall --globals-only option dumps the cluster-wide data alone [3].

rows.question: My text dump restore keeps running after SQL errors. Which psql variable makes it stop and exit with status 3?
rows.answer:
The ON_ERROR_STOP variable. By default the psql script continues to execute after an SQL error; running psql with ON_ERROR_STOP set makes psql exit with an exit status of 3 if an SQL error occurs [1]:

psql -X --set ON_ERROR_STOP=on dbname < dumpfile

Either way, you will only have a partially restored database. Alternatively, pass -1 or --single-transaction to psql so the whole dump is restored as a single transaction (either fully completed or fully rolled back) [1].

rows.question: What exit code does GNU tar 1.16 or later return when a file changed during the backup?
rows.answer: GNU tar versions 1.16 and later exit with 1 if a file was changed during the backup (and 2 for other errors) [1].

rows.question: If template1 has been customized, which template must the empty database be created from before restoring a pg_dump?
rows.answer: template0. Dumps produced by pg_dump are relative to template0, so if you are using a customized template1 you must create the empty database from template0 (e.g., with createdb -T template0 dbname) before restoring [1][2].

rows.question: What happens if the file system holding pg_wal/ fills up because archiving keeps failing?
rows.answer: If the file system containing pg_wal/ fills up, PostgreSQL will do a PANIC shutdown. No committed transactions will be lost, but the database will remain offline until you free some space [1].

rows.question: What is the first step when recovering from a continuous archive backup?
rows.answer: The first step is to stop the server, if it's running [1].

rows.question: Which file do I create in the cluster data directory to make the server start recovery?
rows.answer: Create a file named recovery.signal in the cluster data directory (after setting the recovery configuration settings in postgresql.conf). When you then start the server, it goes into recovery mode and reads through the archived WAL files it needs [1].

rows.question: What value should archive_timeout be set to so WAL segments are archived at least every few minutes?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What is the maximum recommended input-to-output differential voltage for the LM317?
rows.answer: The maximum recommended input-to-output differential voltage (VI - VO) is 40 V (minimum 3 V) [1].

rows.question: What is the typical current out of the ADJUST pin?
rows.answer: The only figure the extracts give is in the LM317 datasheet overview: "A 100μA current from the ADJUST pin represents an error term"; the LM317 is designed to minimize the IADJUST current and make it constant with line and load changes [1]. The extracts do not include the electrical characteristics table row that would give a separate typical (TYP) adjustment pin current value.

rows.question: How much load current must I draw (maximum spec) to keep the regulator in regulation with 40 V across it?
rows.answer: The minimum load current specification at (VIN - VOUT) = 40V, over the full operating temperature range, is 10 mA maximum (3.5 mA typical), so draw at least 10 mA of load current to guarantee regulation [5]. This matches the recommended minimum output current of 0.01 A [7].

rows.question: What is the package designator for the 4-pin SOT-223 version?
rows.answer: DCY - the 4-pin SOT-223 package of the Texas Instruments LM317 is designated DCY [2][3][4].

rows.question: The regulator sits more than six inches from the input filter capacitors. What minimum input bypass capacitor do I fit?
rows.answer: Fit an input bypass capacitor of 0.1μF or greater; it can be of any type, and is needed for stability when the LM317 is more than six inches from the input filter capacitors [1].

rows.question: How do I use the PCB as a heat sink for the TO-263 or SOT-223 package?
rows.reference: solder the tab of the package to the plane
rows.answer: The TO-263 (KTT) and SOT-223 (DCY) packages use a copper plane on the PCB and the PCB itself as a heat sink. To optimize the heat sinking ability of the plane and PCB, solder the tab of the package to the plane [1].

rows.question: In the heat sink equation, what does θCH represent?
rows.reference: thermal resistance of the contact area between the device case and the heat sink surface
rows.answer: In the LM317 datasheet, θCH is the thermal resistance of the contact area between the device case and the heat sink surface [2].

rows.question: What is the risk of running the legacy chip at its absolute maximum junction temperature of 150°C?
rows.answer: Operating the legacy chip at the absolute maximum TJ of 150°C potentially affects reliability [1][3]. More generally, exposure to absolute-maximum-rated conditions for extended periods may affect device reliability, and stresses beyond the absolute maximum ratings may cause permanent damage to the device [2].

rows.question: At what junction temperature does the LM317's internal thermal shutdown trip?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What is the Vin (max) of the LM317?
rows.answer: The extracts do not give a standalone absolute VIN (max) figure; the input limit is specified as the input-to-output differential voltage (VI - VO), which has a maximum of 40 V (minimum 3 V) in the LM317 Recommended Operating Conditions [5]. The electrical characteristics are likewise specified for 3V ≤ (VIN - VOUT) ≤ 40V [1]. The output voltage range is 1.25 V to 37 V [5].

rows.question: What is the Vin (min) of the LM317?
rows.answer: The extracts do not list a single absolute VIN (min) figure; the input is specified relative to the output. The recommended minimum input-to-output differential voltage (VI - VO) is 3 V (maximum 40 V) [3], and the electrical characteristics are specified for 3V ≤ (VIN - VOUT) ≤ 40V [1]. So the minimum input voltage is the output voltage plus 3 V; with the minimum output voltage of 1.25 V [3], that works out to 4.25 V.

rows.question: What is the Iout (max) of the LM317?
rows.answer: The maximum output current of the LM317 is 1.5A (IO Output current MAX 1.5 A in the Recommended Operating Conditions; IOMAX = 1.5A, i.e. 1500mA, in the electrical characteristics test conditions) [4][7][2].

rows.question: What is the Vout (max) of the LM317?
rows.answer: The maximum output voltage (VO) of the LM317 is 37 V, per the Recommended Operating Conditions (output voltage MIN 1.25 V, MAX 37 V) [6].

rows.question: What is the Vout (min) of the LM317?
rows.answer: The minimum output voltage (VO) of the LM317 is 1.25 V (recommended operating conditions: MIN 1.25 V, MAX 37 V) [5].

rows.question: What is the Load capacitance (min) of the LM317?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What is the Operating temperature range of the LM317?
rows.answer: The recommended operating virtual junction temperature (TJ) of the LM317 is 0 °C to 125 °C [6]; the device comparison table likewise lists a recommended operating temperature of 0 to 125 °C for both the legacy chip and the new chip [3]. For the legacy chip, the absolute maximum operating virtual junction temperature range is -65 to 150 °C [4].

rows.question: What installation torque do I use on a 1/4-28 bolt with an AN310 tension nut when the manufacturer gives no value?
rows.answer: Use Table 7-1, which gives the recommended torque when a specific torque is not supplied by the manufacturer [1]. For a 1/4-28 (fine thread) bolt with a tension type nut (MS20365 and AN310, 40,000 psi in bolts), the recommended installation torque is 50-70 inch-pounds; the maximum allowable tightening torque for AN310 nuts at that size is 100 inch-pounds [4]. The values are derived from oil free cadmium plated threads [4].

rows.question: What's the minimum prevailing torque a reused 5/8-11 self-locking nut must still have?
rows.answer: 20 inch-pounds. FAA AC 43.13-1B Table 7-2 (minimum prevailing torque values for reused self-locking nuts), coarse thread series, lists 5/8 - 11 at 20 inch-pounds [1]. Self-locking nuts should be replaced when they are no longer capable of maintaining the minimum prevailing torque [2].

rows.question: What is the minimum breaking strength of 1/8 inch 7 x 19 MIL-W-83420 Comp A control cable?
rows.answer: 2,000 pounds (LBS) minimum breaking strength for 1/8 inch 7 x 19 MIL-W-83420 Comp A cable (Table 7-3) [1].

rows.question: What do I add to the desired torque to get the final torque reading?
rows.answer: Add the friction drag torque to the desired torque. The sum is the "final torque," which should register on the indicator or setting for a snap-over type torque wrench [1].

rows.question: The wrench chatters and jerks as I reach final torque. What should I do?
rows.reference: back off the nut and retorque
rows.answer: If chattering or a jerking motion occurs during final torque, back off the nut and retorque. Apply a smooth even pull when applying torque pressure [2].

rows.question: The castle nut slots won't line up with the cotter pin hole without going past maximum torque. What's the fix?
rows.reference: change washer or nut and try again
rows.answer: When installing a castle nut, start alignment with the cotter pin hole at the minimum recommended torque plus friction drag torque. Do not exceed the maximum torque plus the friction drag. If the hole and nut castellation do not align, change the washer or nut and try again; exceeding the maximum recommended torque is not recommended [1].

rows.question: Above what temperature must cadmium-plated nuts not be used?
rows.answer: Per FAA AC 43.13-1B, cadmium-plated nuts are restricted to use in temperatures not exceeding 450 °F. Above 450 °F the cadmium will diffuse into the base material, causing it to become very brittle and subject to early failure [2]. Cadmium plating is likewise not recommended in applications where the temperature exceeds 450 °F [4].

rows.question: Which MS part number supersedes the AN73-AN81 drilled head bolts for fine thread?
rows.answer: MS20073 supersedes the AN73 through AN81 drilled head bolts for fine thread bolts (MS20074 is the superseding part for coarse thread bolts) [1].

rows.question: How many twists per inch should .032 inch safety wire have?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: How much fuel does the tank on the 3 kW TQG hold?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What is the engine oil capacity?
rows.answer: The engine oil capacity is 1.2 quarts (1.1 liters) [2].

rows.question: What's the longest I can crank the engine on the starter before I have to stop and wait?
rows.answer: Do not crank the engine for more than 15 seconds - damage to the starter motor can occur. Wait 15 seconds before attempting to crank again. If the engine does not run after the third attempt, refer to Troubleshooting [1].

rows.question: After opening the circuit interrupter for shutdown, how long should the set run before I put the switch to STOP?
rows.answer: After placing the CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER switch in the OPEN position, allow the unit to run in this condition for approximately 3-5 minutes to cool down the engine, then place the START / RUN / STOP switch in the STOP position to shut down the generator set (and then pull out the DC CIRCUIT BREAKER) [2].

rows.question: Engine won't crank and the DC circuit breaker is tripped. What do I do?
rows.answer:
If the DC CIRCUIT BREAKER is tripped, reset it by depressing the pushbutton [1].

The other "engine will not crank" checks given are [1]:
- Check that the EMERGENCY STOP switch is not engaged; pull out the switch to disengage.
- Check that the START / RUN / STOP switch is in the START position; place the switch in START position.
- Check the malfunction indicator module for a system fault light; refer to the applicable troubleshooting procedure for the fault condition.
- Check battery wires for proper / secure connection; tighten connections.
- If still not corrected, refer the trouble to unit level maintenance.

rows.question: The set runs but won't build up to rated voltage. What is the first thing to check?
rows.reference: GROUND FAULT CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER (GFCI) is not tripped
rows.answer:
Per TM 9-6115-639-13, the first check is that the GROUND FAULT CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER (GFCI) is not tripped; reset the GFCI by depressing the button [1].

If that does not correct it, the following checks are, in order: check that the VOLTAGE ADJUST rheostat is properly set (adjust the rheostat to achieve rated voltage); check that the voltage selector switch access door is fully closed and secured (close and secure the access door); then refer the trouble to unit level maintenance [1].

rows.question: Engine starts and then stops, and there is water in the fuel filter / water separator. How do I fix it?
rows.reference: Drain water from filter separator by turning valve
rows.answer:
Under "Engine starts and stops" (US Army TM 9-6115-639-13), check for water in the fuel filter / water separator (refer to para. 3-8) and drain the water from the filter separator by turning the valve. If that does not correct it, refer the trouble to unit level maintenance [1].

The other checks listed for this symptom are: check that electrical connections are properly tightened (tighten connections), and inspect for crimped, pinched, or leaking fuel lines (straighten flexible fuel lines; refer to unit level maintenance if a fuel line is damaged) [1].

rows.question: What is the reference designation of the CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER switch?
rows.answer: The CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER switch is reference designation S5 [1].

rows.question: During before-operation PMCS of the control box, how do I run the fault lamp test?
rows.reference: Depress FAULT RESET / PUSH TEST switch
rows.answer: Conduct the fault lamp test by depressing the FAULT RESET / PUSH TEST switch (refer to para. 3-6) [1]. In the US Army TM 9-6115-639-13 operator PMCS table this is item 3 (Before), control box and output panel, step b: inspect switches, meters, indicators, and terminals, then conduct the fault lamp test [1]. The generator set is not fully mission capable if the fault indicator is defective or the lamp does not light [5].

rows.question: What is the PREHEAT switch for?
rows.answer: The PREHEAT switch (S18) is a two-position switch that controls the engine preheat system [1]. The ON position sends a signal to engine preheat contactor K13 to energize the engine air heater; it is used during cold weather operation. The OFF position de-energizes the engine air heater, halting engine preheat operations [2].

rows.question: What torque do the cylinder head bolts get tightened to?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What is the NSN for the MEP-831A generator set?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What is the rated voltage for the XFD12 model?
rows.answer: The rated voltage of the XFD12 is D.C. 18 V [2].

rows.question: What is the net weight of the XFD12 model when using a BL1815N battery cartridge?
rows.answer: With a BL1815N battery cartridge (the BL1815N / BL1820B column of the specifications), the net weight of the XFD12 is 1.5 kg (3.4 lbs); with the BL1830, BL1830B, BL1840B, BL1850B or BL1860B it is 1.8 kg (3.9 lbs). The weight is with battery cartridge, according to EPTA-Procedure 01/2003 [1].

rows.question: What should I use to wipe dirt off the lens of the lamp?
rows.reference: Use a dry cloth to wipe the dirt off the lens of\nthe lamp.
rows.answer: Use a dry cloth to wipe the dirt off the lens of the lamp (Makita XFD12). Be careful not to scratch the lens of the lamp, or it may lower the illumination [1].

rows.question: What is used to secure the hook to the tool housing?
rows.answer: A screw. The hook is inserted into a groove in the tool housing on either side and then secured with a screw [1].

rows.question: How do I perform a screwdriving operation with this tool?
rows.reference:
Place the point of the driver bit in the screw head and
apply pressure to the tool. Start the tool slowly and then
increase the speed gradually. Release the switch trigger
as soon as the clutch cuts in.
rows.answer:
Screwdriving operation (Makita XFD12) [1]:
1. First adjust the adjusting ring to the proper torque level for your work (CAUTION).
2. Place the point of the driver bit in the screw head and apply pressure to the tool. Make sure the driver bit is inserted straight in the screw head, or the screw and/or driver bit may be damaged (CAUTION).
3. Start the tool slowly and then increase the speed gradually.
4. Release the switch trigger as soon as the clutch cuts in.
NOTE: When driving a wood screw, pre-drill a pilot hole 2/3 the diameter of the screw; it makes driving easier and prevents splitting of the workpiece [1].

rows.question: What is the function of the adjusting ring on the tool?
rows.reference: The fastening torque can be adjusted in 22 levels by turning the adjusting ring.
rows.answer: The adjusting ring is used to adjust the fastening torque. The fastening torque can be adjusted in 22 levels by turning the adjusting ring and aligning the graduations with the arrow on the tool body. Minimum fastening torque is at 1 and maximum torque is at the marking. The clutch will slip at various torque levels when set at the numbers 1 to 21; the clutch does not work at the marking [2]. For screwdriving, adjust the adjusting ring to the proper torque level for your work [4]; for drilling, turn the adjusting ring so that the arrow points to the marking [3].

rows.question: What is the purpose of the hook that can be installed on the tool?
rows.reference: The hook is convenient for temporarily hanging the tool.
rows.answer: The hook is convenient for temporarily hanging the tool. It can be installed on either side of the tool [1].

rows.question: What specific handling instruction is given to prevent damage to the battery cartridge?
rows.reference: Be careful not to drop or strike battery.
rows.answer: Hold the tool and the battery cartridge firmly when installing or removing the battery cartridge; failure to hold them firmly may cause them to slip off your hands and result in damage to the tool and battery cartridge and a personal injury [1]. The extracts also say: do not install the battery cartridge forcibly (if it does not slide in easily, it is not being inserted correctly) [1], and be careful not to drop or strike the battery [3].

rows.question: What is the specific warranty period covering the lithium-ion battery cartridge if purchased separately?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: Are there any specific safety guidelines for operating this drill in ambient temperatures below 0 °C (32 °F)?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What type of batteries are stipulated for use to prevent potential hazards like fire or injury?
rows.answer: For the Makita XFD12, only genuine Makita batteries should be used. Use of non-genuine Makita batteries, or batteries that have been altered, may result in the battery bursting causing fires, personal injury and damage, and will also void the Makita warranty for the tool and charger [2]. The general safety warnings likewise say to use power tools only with specifically designated battery packs, because use of any other battery packs may create a risk of injury and fire [1].

rows.question: How do I install the battery cartridge into the tool correctly?
rows.reference: To install the battery cartridge, align the tongue on the battery cartridge with the groove in the housing and slip it into place. Insert it all the way until it locks in place with a little click.
rows.answer:
- Always switch off the tool before installing the battery cartridge, and hold the tool and the battery cartridge firmly [1]. Before installing, check that the switch trigger actuates properly and returns to the "OFF" position when released [4].
- Align the tongue on the battery cartridge with the groove in the housing and slip it into place [1].
- Insert it all the way until it locks in place with a little click [1][7].
- If you can see the red indicator on the upper side of the button, it is not locked completely; install it fully until the red indicator cannot be seen, otherwise it may accidentally fall out of the tool and cause injury [1][7].
- Do not install the cartridge forcibly; if it does not slide in easily, it is not being inserted correctly [1].

rows.question: What is the correct procedure for performing a screwdriving operation?
rows.reference: Place the point of the driver bit in the screw head and apply pressure to the tool. Start the tool slowly and then increase the speed gradually. Release the switch trigger as soon as the clutch cuts in.
rows.answer:
Screwdriving operation (Makita XFD12) [1]:
1. Adjust the adjusting ring to the proper torque level for your work (CAUTION).
2. Place the point of the driver bit in the screw head and apply pressure to the tool. Make sure that the driver bit is inserted straight in the screw head, or the screw and/or driver bit may be damaged (CAUTION).
3. Start the tool slowly and then increase the speed gradually.
4. Release the switch trigger as soon as the clutch cuts in.
NOTE: When driving a wood screw, pre-drill a pilot hole 2/3 the diameter of the screw. It makes driving easier and prevents splitting of the workpiece [1].

rows.question: For how long does the front lamp remain illuminated after the switch trigger has been released?
rows.reference: The lamp goes out approximately 10 seconds after releasing the switch trigger.
rows.answer: The lamp goes out approximately 10 seconds after releasing the switch trigger [1]. (If the tool is overheated and the lamp is flashing, the lamp turns off in one minute after the switch trigger is released [1].)

rows.question: What is the recommended temperature range for charging the battery cartridge to ensure safety and battery health?
rows.answer: For the Makita XFD12 battery cartridge: charge the battery cartridge with room temperature at 10 °C - 40 °C (50 °F - 104 °F). Let a hot battery cartridge cool down before charging it [1].

rows.question: How heavy is the drill with the standard battery?
rows.answer: The net weight (with battery cartridge, according to EPTA-Procedure 01/2003) is 1.5 kg (3.4 lbs) or 1.8 kg (3.9 lbs), depending on the standard battery cartridge fitted: the specification lists the cartridges in two groups (BL1815N, BL1820B and BL1830, BL1830B, BL1840B, BL1850B, BL1860B) against those two weights, i.e. 1.5 kg (3.4 lbs) with the first group and 1.8 kg (3.9 lbs) with the second [3].

rows.question: What happens if the tool or battery is operated in a way that draws an abnormally high current?
rows.reference: the tool automatically stops without any indication.
rows.answer: The overload protection operates: the tool automatically stops without any indication. In this situation, turn the tool off and stop the application that caused the tool to become overloaded, then turn the tool on to restart [1]. This is part of the tool/battery protection system, which automatically cuts off power to the motor to extend tool and battery life [7].

rows.question: What could be the consequence of shorting the battery terminals together?
rows.reference: Shorting the battery terminals together may cause burns or a fire.
rows.answer: Shorting the battery terminals together may cause burns or a fire [1]. The Makita battery cartridge safety instructions add that a battery short can cause a large current flow, overheating, possible burns and even a breakdown [6]. For that reason, when the battery pack is not in use keep it away from other metal objects (paper clips, coins, keys, nails, screws or other small metal objects) that can make a connection from one terminal to another [1], and do not touch the terminals with any conductive material or store the cartridge in a container with other metal objects such as nails, coins, etc. [6].

rows.question: What are the risks associated with using non-genuine Makita batteries?
rows.reference: Use of non-genuine Makita batteries, or batteries that\n~~h~~ ave ~~b~~ een a ~~lt~~ ere ~~d~~, may resu ~~lt~~ ~~i~~ n ~~th~~ e ~~b~~ a ~~tt~~ ery ~~b~~ urs ~~ti~~ ng\ncausing fires, personal injury and damage.

rows.question: What is the no-load speed in high (2) setting for the XFD12 model?
rows.answer: The no load speed of the Makita XFD12 in the High (2) setting is 0 - 2,000 /min [2].

rows.question: What type of lubricant is recommended when drilling into metals, excluding iron and brass?
rows.answer: Use a cutting lubricant when drilling metals. The exceptions are iron and brass, which should be drilled dry [1].

rows.question: What type of drill bit is best for drilling in wood?
rows.reference: wood drills equipped with a guide screw
rows.answer: Per the Makita XFD12 manual, when drilling in wood the best results are obtained with wood drills equipped with a guide screw. The guide screw makes drilling easier by pulling the drill bit into the workpiece [1].

rows.question: How do I check the remaining battery capacity if my battery has a "B" at the end of its model number?
rows.reference: Press the check button on the battery cartridge to indicate the remaining battery capacity. The indicator lamps\nlight up for few seconds.
rows.answer: Press the check button on the battery cartridge to indicate the remaining battery capacity. The indicator lamps light up for a few seconds and show the remaining capacity (ranges of 75% to 100%, 50% to 75%, 25% to 50%, 0% to 25%; further indications mean "Charge the battery" or "The battery may have malfunctioned"). This applies only to Makita battery cartridges with "B" at the end of the model number. Note: depending on the conditions of use and the ambient temperature, the indication may differ slightly from the actual capacity [1].

rows.question: Where is the driver bit holder installed?
rows.reference: Fit the driver bit holder into the protrusion at the tool foot\non either right or left side
rows.answer: The driver bit holder (an optional accessory) is fitted into the protrusion at the tool foot, on either the right or left side, and secured with a screw [1].

rows.question: What meaning is assigned to the "V" symbol in the manual's symbol list?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: Under what condition related to previous repairs does the Makita warranty not apply?
rows.reference: repairs have been made or attempted by others:
rows.answer: The warranty does not apply where repairs have been made or attempted by others [1].

rows.question: What is a potential severe consequence if battery electrolyte contacts the eyes?
rows.reference: It may result in loss of your eyesight.
rows.answer: It may result in loss of your eyesight. If electrolyte gets into your eyes, rinse them out with clear water and seek medical attention right away [2]. (Liquid ejected from the battery may also cause irritation or burns; if it contacts eyes, flush with water and additionally seek medical help [1].)

rows.question: When is it recommended to charge a battery cartridge that hasn't been used for an extended period?
rows.reference: Charge the battery cartridge if you do not use\n\nit for a long period (more than six months).

rows.question: As a new user, what are the initial steps I should take to get my first print going?
rows.reference:
1. Read the Safety Instructions carefully (page 8).

2. Place the printer on a flat and stable surface and plug it in. (page 15)

3. If you bought the assembled printer, remove the test print from the print sheet (remove the

sheet, bend it, remove the print), then place the print sheet back. (page 17)

4. Calibrate the printer using the Selftest Wizard. (page 18)

5. Insert the USB drive that came with your printer and print your first object. (page 23)
rows.answer:
For the Original Prusa MK4S, the "Your First Print" chapter covers these steps in order: control the printer, prepare the print sheet for the first print, perform the initial calibration, insert filament, start the first print, and remove the print (plus troubleshooting basic issues and updating the firmware) [1][2].

Details the extracts give:
1. Print sheet / calibration: the print sheet must be installed onto the printer before the calibration. When you first power on the printer, the Selftest (Calibration Wizard) starts and walks you through the initial calibration and all necessary tests to start printing; completing the entire checklist is mandatory. The first thing the wizard performs is the internet setup, which is completely optional and can be skipped (the printer is fully functional offline). The Selftest can also be started manually via LCD menu - Control - Run Full Selftest [4].
2. Insert filament (listed as a step; the extracts do not give the loading procedure) [1].
3. Starting the first print: if you haven't already, clean the print sheet with the enclosed wipe saturated with isopropyl alcohol, or spray a bit of isopropyl alcohol onto the sheet and wipe it clean with a paper towel. Then select one of the test objects from the Print menu (only appears if a USB drive is inserted) and confirm by pressing the rotary knob. The Keychain is recommended. Watch the printer closely during the first print [8].
4. What happens next: the nozzle first preheats to 170 °C independently of the selected filament, then the printer performs Mesh Bed Leveling, and then the object is printed [8].
5. Remove the print afterwards [1].

rows.answer: The primary risk is fire: "Do not leave the printer unattended while it is on!" The printer is equipped with temperature control and several smart safety features, but misuse or unexpected component failure can pose a fire hazard [1].

rows.question: What are the potential safety hazards if obstructions near the printer cause wear on cable sheaths?
rows.reference: Worn cables can pose a risk (electric shock, fire).
rows.answer: Per the Prusa MK4S / MK3.9S manual, obstructions near the printer can cause excessive wear on cable sheaths or the cables themselves, and worn cables can pose a risk of electric shock and fire. For this reason, ensure there is at least 30 cm of space around the printer [1]. Damaged cables can lead to electric shock, so do not use the printer if the power cable is damaged [8].

rows.question: What concentration of isopropyl alcohol is recommended for degreasing the print sheet surface?
rows.reference: Use highly concentrated isopropyl alcohol (90% or more) to degrease the sheet surface.
rows.answer: Highly concentrated isopropyl alcohol of 90% or more (IPA 90%+) is recommended for degreasing the print sheet surface [1][2][3][6]. Do not use products that only contain IPA as one of the components (e.g. hand sanitizers), as they contain other additives [1][2].

rows.question: How do I load filament into the printer?
rows.reference:
1. Cut the end of the filament into a sharp point. Push the filament through the hole in the

filament guide and insert the plastic strand into the opening at the top of the Nextruder. If the
filament sensor is on, the filament will be automatically fed. If the filament sensor is off,
proceed to step 2, otherwise skip to step 3.

2. Select LCD Menu - Filament - Load Filament and confirm with the button.

3. The Preheat menu will automatically appear. Select the material of the filament you want to

insert and confirm the selection.

4. Wait until the nozzle reaches the desired temperature.

5. Select Continue to start feeding the filament. Push the filament into the Nextruder lightly until

you feel that the extruder gear grabbed the filament and is pulling it in.
rows.answer:
Loading filament:
- Prepare a spool of filament (PLA is strongly recommended because it is easy to work with). Make sure the end of the filament is properly secured and place the spool onto the spoolholder on top of the printer's frame [1].
- Carefully unhook the end of the filament strand and do not let go, otherwise the tension in the strand would cause the filament to quickly tangle up. Cut the end of the filament into a sharp point [1].
1. Push the filament through the hole in the filament guide and insert the strand into the opening at the top of the Nextruder. If the filament sensor is on, the filament will be automatically fed (skip to step 3); if the filament sensor is off, proceed to step 2 [1].
2. Select LCD Menu - Filament - Load Filament and confirm with the button [1].
3. The Preheat menu will automatically appear. Select the material of the filament you want to insert and confirm the selection [1].
4. Wait until the nozzle reaches the desired temperature [1].
5. Select Continue to start feeding the filament. Push the filament into the Nextruder lightly until you feel that the extruder gear grabbed the filament and is pulling it in [7].
6. The feed wheel will then push the filament further into the extruder. Once it heats up fully, it will push out a bit of material from the nozzle [7].
- The printer will ask if the color of the extruded filament is okay (Yes / Purge More / Retry). Check if filament is extruded from the nozzle, then: if the filament is extruded and the color is correct, select YES; if it is not extruded or is contaminated with another color, select PURGE MORE (this can be repeated); if it is not extruded and PURGE MORE doesn't help, repeat the loading procedure by choosing RETRY [7].

rows.question: What is the Nextruder on the Original Prusa MK4S?
rows.reference: Nextruder - Our new next-generation extruder with a planetary gearbox and LoadCell sensor.
rows.answer: The Nextruder is Prusa's new next-generation extruder with a planetary gearbox and LoadCell sensor [1]. It is moved up and down by the Z-axis (Z-axis motors) and left and right along the X-axis by the X-axis stepper motor [1]. It contains an electronics board whose connectors should be checked every 600-800 hours of printing [6], and a Nextruder to V6 nozzle adapter is available so V6-compatible nozzles can be used [4].

rows.question: What does 'Stealth Mode' do on this 3D printer?
rows.reference: With Stealth Mode enabled, the firmware limits the acceleration, feedrate, and jerk values,\nresulting in reduced printer noise.
rows.answer: With Stealth Mode enabled, the firmware limits the acceleration, feedrate, and jerk values, resulting in reduced printer noise. Due to these limits, the overall printing time is slightly increased. You can switch between Normal and Stealth Mode anytime, even during printing; after enabling, Stealth Mode is activated once several G-code commands in the buffer (printer memory) are processed. It is enabled in Settings -> Stealth Mode [1].

rows.question: As a Safety Officer, what's the primary safety concern if a user reports using a damaged power cable with the printer?
rows.reference: Damaged cables are a safety risk risk of electric shock.
rows.answer: The primary concern is electric shock. Do not use the printer if the power cable is damaged - damaged cables can lead to electric shock [1]. If the cables are damaged, stop using the device immediately and replace the cables; damaged cables are a safety risk - risk of electric shock [2].

rows.question: What is this handbook for?
rows.reference: FOR THE ORIGINAL PRUSA MK4S 3D PRINTER
rows.answer: It is the 3D Printing Handbook (Official Instructions) for the Original Prusa MK4S 3D printer [1][2]. In it you learn everything you need to set up your printer, use it, perform routine maintenance, and more [1]. It primarily references the Original Prusa MK4S, but the instructions are equally applicable to the MK3.9S, as the two are virtually identical from the user's perspective [1]. (Assembly instructions are found separately at prusa.io/mk4s [1].)

rows.question: What are the first steps I need to take to make my first print?
rows.reference:
1. Read the Safety Instructions carefully (page 8).

2. Place the printer on a flat and stable surface and plug it in. (page 15)

3. If you bought the assembled printer, remove the test print from the print sheet (remove the

sheet, bend it, remove the print), then place the print sheet back. (page 17)

4. Calibrate the printer using the Selftest Wizard. (page 18)

5. Insert the USB drive that came with your printer and print your first object. (page 23)
rows.answer:
From the Prusa MK4S / MK3.9S manual extracts, the first steps are:

1. Prepare the print sheet. If you ordered a pre-assembled printer, a print sheet with a test print is already installed and the test print must be removed before proceeding: remove the print sheet and carefully bend it on both sides, turn it by 90° and repeat the bending until the print separates, then place the sheet back on the printer. Make sure there is no debris on the heatbed before installing the sheet, and do not drag the sheet while it is attached by the magnets - lift it by the front two corners to readjust it [8].
2. Install the sheet on the heatbed: make sure it is perfectly clean (never print directly on the heated bed), align the rear cutout with the locking pins on the back of the heated bed, hold the sheet by the front two corners and slowly lay it down. For the first print it is enough to wipe the bed with the supplied cleaning wipes soaked with isopropyl alcohol; do not touch the surface afterward [4].
3. Power on the printer and complete the Selftest (Calibration wizard). The print sheet must be installed before the calibration. The wizard starts when you first power on the printer and walks you through the initial calibration and all necessary tests; completing the entire checklist is mandatory. Its first step, the internet setup, is optional and can be skipped. The Selftest can also be started manually via LCD menu - Control - Run Full Selftest [2].
4. Start the first print: if you haven't already, clean the print sheet with the enclosed wipe saturated with isopropyl alcohol (or spray a bit of isopropyl alcohol on the sheet and wipe it clean with a paper towel). Then select one of the test objects from the Print menu (it only appears if a USB drive is inserted) - the Keychain is recommended - and confirm by pressing the rotary knob. Watch the printer closely during the first print [5].
5. The printer then preheats the nozzle to 170 °C (independently of the selected filament), performs Mesh Bed Leveling, and subsequently prints the object [5].

rows.question: What is the supported filament diameter for the MK4S?
rows.answer: The supported filament diameter for the Original Prusa MK4S is 1.75 mm [1].

rows.question: What should I use to degrease the print sheet surface?
rows.reference: Use highly concentrated isopropyl alcohol (90% or more) to degrease the sheet surface.
rows.answer:
Use highly concentrated isopropyl alcohol (IPA, 90% or more) to degrease the sheet surface; before printing, clean the print sheet surface with a cloth moistened with isopropyl alcohol [1][3][5]. Drop a small amount of the agent onto a clean paper towel and wipe the print surface, preferably while the print sheet is cold [8]. Do not use products that contain IPA as only one of the components (e.g. hand sanitizers / dermatological hand products), because their additives may negatively affect the printing plate, and do not wash the sheet under running water, as it may corrode [1][3].

By sheet type [3]:
- Smooth PEI sheet: Isopropyl alcohol 90%+ is the best option; warm water with a few drops of dish soap can be used if IPA does not remove residues like sugar; acetone only occasionally for thorough cleaning [3].
- Textured powder-coated sheet: Isopropyl alcohol 90%+ is best for degreasing; never use acetone [3][6][1].
- Satin sheet: 90% isopropyl alcohol is the best degreaser; do not use acetone, as it will damage the surface [3][5][1].

rows.question: What might happen if I accidentally release the end of the filament?
rows.reference: If you accidentally release the end of the filament, it can easily tangle and knot.
rows.answer: The filament can easily tangle and knot [1]. The tension in the strand makes it retract quickly onto the spool and tangle up [5][2]. This is a risk during printing: a knot can form on the strand, which will inevitably lead to a failed print [2]. To fix it, remove the spool from the spoolholder, unwind the filament strand until you find the crossed section, fix it and wind the filament back onto the spool [2].

rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What should I use to degrease the smooth PEI print sheet?
rows.reference: Isopropyl alcohol 90%+ (IPA) is the best option for degreasing.
rows.answer: Use highly concentrated isopropyl alcohol (IPA), 90% or more - it is the best option for degreasing the smooth PEI print sheet [4][3]. Do not use products that merely contain IPA as one component (e.g. hand sanitizers / dermatological hand products), because they contain other additives [3][4]. If IPA does not remove residues such as sugar, use warm water with a few drops of dish soap, and acetone can be used occasionally for thorough cleaning [4][2].

rows.question: What material is recommended for smoothing PVB prints?
rows.answer: Isopropyl alcohol (IPA). PVB can be easily smoothed with isopropyl alcohol [1]; models can be smoothed in IPA vapors, by immersing into an IPA bath, or by directly applying IPA on the object surface (by using a sprayer or brush) [4]. For translucent prints to be smoothed later with isopropyl alcohol, a bigger nozzle (0.8mm) and the "Spiral vase" mode in PrusaSlicer are recommended [2].

rows.question: What is the procedure for cleaning a clogged nozzle using an acupuncture needle?
rows.reference:
1. Heat the nozzle to the appropriate temperature for the filament material you are printing with

or slightly above. First, feed the filament, then insert an acupuncture needle (included in the
package) or thin wire (0.3-0.35 mm) into the nozzle from the bottom to a depth of about 1-2
cm. Use protective gloves in case material suddenly starts to come out of the nozzle.

2. Select the Load Filament option from the LCD menu and check that the nozzle is actually

extruding the filament.

3. Again insert the wire or acupuncture needle into the nozzle and repeat the whole procedure

several times. If the filament is being extruded correctly, the nozzle is clean.
rows.answer:
Do not touch the nozzle during this procedure - it is hot and there is a risk of burning yourself. To better access the extruder during cleaning, raise the extruder to the top of the Z-axis in the LCD menu - Control - Movement - Z Axis [2].

Procedure [1]:
1. Heat the nozzle to the appropriate temperature for the filament material you are printing with, or slightly above. First, feed the filament, then insert the acupuncture needle (included in the package) or thin wire (0.3-0.35 mm) into the nozzle from the bottom to a depth of about 1-2 cm. Use protective gloves in case material suddenly starts to come out of the nozzle.
2. Select the Load Filament option from the LCD menu and check that the nozzle is actually extruding the filament.
3. Again insert the wire or acupuncture needle into the nozzle and repeat the whole procedure several times. If the filament is being extruded correctly, the nozzle is clean.

If the filament still doesn't come out and the nozzle is clogged, you can perform a cold pull method to clean the insides of the nozzle; the Cold Pull wizard is in the printer's LCD Menu [1].

rows.question: What should I do if the LoadCell calibration fails during the first print setup?
rows.reference: This usually happens when you tap the nozzle too briefly or with not enough force.\nRepeat the calibration and push the nozzle a bit harder.
rows.answer: This usually happens when you tap the nozzle too briefly or with not enough force. Repeat the calibration and push the nozzle a bit harder [1].

rows.question: What is likely the problem if I hear the extruder gear clicking during purging?
rows.reference: If you hear the extruder gear clicking during Purging, it may be a sign the nozzle is\nblocked.
rows.answer: Per the Prusa MK4S / MK3.9S manual, if you hear the extruder gear clicking during Purging, it may be a sign that the nozzle is blocked. The manual directs you to the Troubleshooting chapters of the handbook or to help.prusa3d.com for a detailed solution [1].

rows.question: What precaution must be taken before performing printer calibration regarding the print sheet?
rows.reference: The print sheet must be installed onto the printer before the calibration!!!
rows.answer:
The print sheet must be installed onto the printer before the calibration (Selftest / Calibration Wizard) [2].

Related precautions in the extracts: on a pre-assembled printer, the test print on the installed print sheet must be removed before proceeding (remove the sheet, bend it on both sides, turn it by 90° and repeat until the print separates, then place the sheet back on the printer), and make sure there is no debris on the heatbed before installing the print sheet, as it could throw off the first layer calibration or even damage the printer [1].

rows.question: What crucial safety rule applies to the printer when it is powered on?
rows.reference: Do not leave the printer unattended while it is on!
rows.answer:
Do not leave the printer unattended while it is on - despite temperature control and several smart safety features, misuse or unexpected component failure can pose a fire hazard [3]. Also, never interfere with the print area when the printer is in operation, and prevent foreign objects from entering the print area and the area around the printer [3].

In addition, never, under any circumstances, disconnect electrical parts while the printer is on (this includes disconnecting the Nextruder from the motherboard, the heated bed, the LCD, and others); always turn off the printer before disconnecting electrical parts [2].

rows.question: What's the power supply voltage range for the printer?
rows.answer: The extracts do not give a voltage range as such; they state that the Prusa printer can only be powered through a standard 230 VAC, 50 Hz or 110 VAC, 60 Hz power outlet, and that alternative sources must never be used [8].

rows.question: What specific lubricant is provided with the MK4S for bearing maintenance?
rows.answer: The package includes "Prusa lubricant for bearings" [2]. For bearing maintenance it is the lubricant in the white tube in the package: apply a little of the included lubricant on the smooth rods (after cleaning them with a paper towel) and move the axis back and forth a couple of times [4].

rows.question: How do I correctly install the flexible print sheet onto the heatbed?
rows.reference: Attach the sheet by first aligning the rear cutout with the locking pins on the back of the\nheated bed (marked in orange in the picture above). Hold the sheet by the front two corners and\nslowly lay it down onto the heated bed - watch your fingers!
rows.answer:
To install the flexible print sheet onto the heatbed (Prusa MK4S / MK3.9S):

1. Make sure the sheet is perfectly clean before installing it, and make sure there is no debris on the heatbed - debris could throw off the first layer calibration or possibly even damage the printer [1][2].
2. Align the rear cutout of the sheet with the two locking pins on the back of the heated bed (the pins fit exactly into the cutout of the print sheet) [1].
3. Hold the sheet by the front two corners and slowly lay it down onto the heated bed - watch your fingers. The sheet is held in place by strong high-temperature magnets embedded in the heatbed, so be careful when placing it to avoid injury [1][3].

Additional points:
- Do not drag or move the print sheet while it is attached by the magnets - friction could scratch and damage the heatbed. If you need to readjust it, always lift it up by grabbing the front two corners, adjust its position and then place it back down [2][3].
- Never print directly on the heated bed [1].
- For your first print it is enough to wipe the sheet with the supplied cleaning wipes soaked with isopropyl alcohol; do not touch the surface of the sheet afterward [1].

rows.question: What does the rotary knob next to the LCD screen do?
rows.reference: Rotate\nthe knob to select items on the screen and press it to confirm your selection.
rows.answer: On the Prusa MK4S, the rotary knob is the printer's main control device (alongside the touchscreen): rotate the knob to select items on the screen and press it to confirm your selection [1][5]. The Reset button is located directly under the rotary knob [1][5]. The knob is also used, for example, to confirm firmware flashing by selecting FLASH and pressing it [4], and to adjust print speed up or down in LCD Menu - Tune - Speed [8].

rows.question: What is the purpose of the 'Brim' feature in PrusaSlicer?
rows.reference: The brim serves to increase adhesion to the bed, reducing the risk of warping.
rows.answer: The brim serves to increase adhesion to the bed, reducing the risk of warping: a wider first layer is printed around the model, which makes sense especially if the model only touches the bed in a small area [1]. It increases the area of the first layer [4]. It is enabled by checking the "Brim" box in the menu in the right column of PrusaSlicer, and after printing the brim can usually be removed easily by hand, or with a knife or scalpel [1].

rows.question: Is it safe to leave the 3D printer unattended while it is on?
rows.reference: Do not leave the printer unattended while it is on!
rows.answer: No. The Prusa MK4S manual states: "Do not leave the printer unattended while it is on!" The printer is equipped with temperature control and several smart safety features, but misuse or unexpected component failure can pose a fire hazard [1].

rows.question: What app should I download to use with the Mavic Pro?
rows.reference: Be sure to use the DJI GO TM 4 app or other apps compatible with DJI aircraft during flight.
rows.answer: Download the DJI GO 4 app (or use other apps compatible with DJI aircraft) for use during flight; scan the QR code in the manual to download the latest version [1]. The Android version is compatible with Android 4.4 or later and the iOS version with iOS 9.0 or later [1]. DJI GO 4 is the mobile application used to control the gimbal, camera, and other aircraft functions [5]. (Separately, the DJI Assistant 2 can be downloaded at http://www.dji.com/mavic/download [2].)

rows.question: What's the maximum video resolution the Mavic Pro can capture?
rows.answer: The Mavic Pro captures video up to 4K at 30 fps (4K video at up to 30 frames per second) [1][4].

rows.question: What is the maximum flight speed of the Mavic Pro?
rows.reference: Mavic Pro boasts a maximum flight speed of 40 mph (65 kph)
rows.answer:
The Mavic Pro's maximum flight speed is 40 mph (65 kph) [1]; the specifications list Max Speed as 40.4 mph (65 kph) in Sport Mode without wind [8], and S-mode (Sport) is where maximum speed is increased to 40mph (65kph) [5].

Lower limits apply in other modes:
- P-mode with the Forward Vision System enabled and sufficient lighting: 22 mph (36 kph); with forward obstacle sensing disabled: 36 mph (58 kph) [2].
- Tripod Mode: limited to 2.2 mph (3.6 kph) [4].
- When using Wi-Fi: 9mph (14kph) [7].

rows.question: How do I attach the propellers correctly?
rows.reference:
Attach the white ringed propellers to the mounting base with white marks. Press the propeller down onto

the mounting plate and rotate in the lock direction until it is secured. Attach the other propellers to the

mounting base without marks.
rows.answer:
Attaching the propellers (DJI Mavic Pro) [1][2]:
1. Attach the white ringed propellers to the mounting base with white marks.
2. Press the propeller down onto the mounting plate and rotate in the lock direction until it is secured.
3. Attach the other (unmarked) propellers to the mounting bases without marks.
4. Unfold all the propeller blades [1].

Use only DJI approved propellers; the white ring and unmarked propellers indicate where they should be attached and in which direction they should spin [4]. Do not mix propeller types, and check that the propellers and motors are installed correctly and firmly before every flight [3][5].

rows.question: What is the function of the Flight Mode Switch on the controller?
rows.answer:
The Flight Mode Switch is used to select/change the aircraft's flight mode, switching between P-mode and S-mode [2][3][4].
- P-mode (Positioning): works best when the GPS signal is strong; the aircraft uses GPS and the Forward and Downward Vision Systems to locate itself, automatically stabilize, and navigate between obstacles. Advanced features such as TapFly and ActiveTrack are enabled [3].
- S-mode (Sport): handling is adjusted to enhance maneuverability and speed; maximum speed is increased to 40mph (65kph) and the Forward Vision System is disabled [3].
The Flight Mode is locked in P-mode by default regardless of switch position; to switch modes, enable "Multiple Flight Modes" in Camera view in the DJI GO 4 app, then toggle the switch to P and then to S to fly in Sport Mode (this must be done every time before using S-mode, since the aircraft flies in P-mode by default after powering on) [3]. In dual remote controller use, only the Primary remote controller can switch the flight mode; the switch is disabled on the Secondary remote controller [1].

rows.question: What happens if the GPS signal is weak and the Vision System is unavailable?
rows.reference: The aircraft will revert to ATTI mode when GPS signal is weak, or when the compass experiences interfer­\nence where the Vision System is unavailable.
rows.answer:
On the DJI Mavic Pro, the aircraft reverts to ATTI mode when the GPS signal is weak, or when the compass experiences interference, where the Vision System is unavailable. In ATTI mode the aircraft is easily affected by its surroundings, which may result in horizontal shifting [2]. Likewise in Tripod Mode, if GPS signal is lost and the vision system cannot function, it automatically switches to Atti mode; flight speed will increase and the aircraft cannot hover in place [6].

Related limits: when the GPS signal is weak and the Downward Vision System is inactivated, height is restricted to 98 feet (30 meters) [3], and the aircraft cannot return to the Home Point when the GPS signal is weak or unavailable [1][4].

rows.question: When is Failsafe RTH automatically activated?
rows.reference: Failsafe RTH\nwill be automatically activated if the remote controller signal is lost for a specified amount of time (3\nseconds when using the remote controller and 20 seconds when using Wi-Fi).
rows.answer: If the Home Point was successfully recorded and the compass is functioning normally, Failsafe RTH is automatically activated if the remote controller signal is lost for a specified amount of time: 3 seconds when using the remote controller and 20 seconds when using Wi-Fi [1].

rows.question: What are the lighting condition limits for TapFly to work?
rows.reference: provided that the lighting is appropriate (< 300 lux) nor too bright (> 10,000 lux).
rows.answer: TapFly's obstacle avoidance (automatically avoiding obstacles it sees, or braking and hovering) works provided that the lighting is appropriate; the only figure printed in the extracts is "10,000 lux" [1]. The manual also says to be extra cautious when flying in dark "( 10,000 lux)" environments [3]. The comparison symbols and any lower (dark) lux figure are missing from the extract text, so the only limit value the extracts give is 10,000 lux [1][3].

rows.question: What kind of propellers should I use with the Mavic Pro?
rows.reference: Use only DJI approved propellers with your Mavic Pro.
rows.answer: Use only DJI approved propellers with your Mavic Pro [1][2] - ONLY use original DJI propellers for a better and safer flight experience [2]. Do not mix propeller types, and do not use aged, chipped, or broken propellers [2]. The propellers come as white ring and unmarked types, which indicate where they should be attached and in which direction they spin [1]: white ringed propellers go on the mounting bases with white marks, and the other propellers on the mounting bases without marks [3].

rows.question: What is the warranty period for the Mavic Pro?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: How long can the Mavic Pro Platinum fly for?
rows.reference: extended max flight time of 30 min
rows.answer: The Mavic Pro Platinum has a maximum flight time of 30 minutes (compared with 27 minutes for the Mavic Pro), tested in 0 wind at a consistent 15.5 mph (25 kph); this value should be taken for reference only [1][3]. Its maximum hovering time is 27 minutes (0 wind) [1].

rows.question: What is the capacity and voltage of the Intelligent Flight Battery?
rows.reference: a capacity of 3830 mAh, a voltage of 11.4 V
rows.answer: The DJI Intelligent Flight Battery has a capacity of 3830 mAh and a voltage of 11.4 V [1][3].

rows.question: What parts should I use to protect the gimbal when the drone isn't in use?
rows.reference: Use the Gimbal Clamp and Gimbal Cover to protect the gimbal when the Mavic Pro is not in use.
rows.answer: Use the Gimbal Clamp and the Gimbal Cover to protect the gimbal when the Mavic Pro is not in use [1].

rows.question: What type of Micro SD card is recommended for saving high-resolution video?
rows.reference: A UHS-1 Micro SD card is recommended
rows.answer: A UHS-1 Micro SD card is recommended, due to their fast read and write speeds allowing you to save high-resolution video data. The Mavic Pro comes with a 16 GB Micro SD card and supports Micro SD cards up to 64 GB [1].

rows.question: What is the procedure for linking a new remote controller?
rows.reference:
1. Turn on the remote controller and connect to the mobile device, and turn on the aircraft. Launch the

DJI GO 4 app.
2. Enter “Camera” and tap on and then tap the “Linking Primary RC” or “Linking Secondary
RC” button to confirm.
3. The remote controller is ready to link.
4. Locate the linking button on the side of the aircraft... Press the link button
rows.answer:
Linking is only required when using a new remote controller for the first time (the remote controller is linked to the aircraft before delivery) [1]. Steps:
1. Turn on the remote controller and connect to the mobile device, and turn on the aircraft [1]. (Toggle the Control Mode switch to RC mode before linking [2].)
2. Launch the DJI GO 4 app [1].
3. Enter "Camera", tap the icon, and then tap the "Linking Primary RC" or "Linking Secondary RC" button to confirm [1]. The remote controller is now ready to link [2].
4. Locate the linking button on the side of the aircraft and press the link button to start linking [2].
5. The Linking Status Indicator will display a solid green once the remote controller is successfully linked to the aircraft, and the LCD screen on the remote controller will display the aircraft's information [2].
Notes: the remote controller will un-link itself from an aircraft if a new remote controller is linked to the same aircraft. In dual remote controller mode, the slave remote controller must be relinked to the aircraft when the master remote controller has been relinked [2].

rows.question: What are the two situations that might cause a gimbal motor error?
rows.reference: (1) The aircraft is placed on uneven ground or the gimbal’s motion is obstructed.\n(2) The gimbal has been subjected to excessive external force, such as a collision.
rows.answer:
For the DJI Mavic Pro, a gimbal motor error may occur in these situations [1]:
1. The aircraft is placed on uneven ground or the gimbal's motion is obstructed.
2. The gimbal has been subjected to excessive external force, such as a collision.

rows.question: On what page can I find information about the 'Intelligent Flight Battery'?
rows.answer: The Intelligent Flight Battery section is on page 28 (heading, introduction and battery functions) [4][6][8]; charging the Intelligent Flight Battery is covered on page 30 [5].

rows.question: What is the correct way to unfold the drone's arms?
rows.reference: 1. Unfold the front arms, followed by the rear arms of the aircraft as shown.\n2. Unfold all propeller blades.
rows.answer:
For the DJI Mavic Pro, all arms are folded on delivery [2]. To unfold them:

1. Unfold the front arms first, followed by the rear arms of the aircraft.
2. Unfold all propeller blades.

Unfold the front arms and the propellers before the rear ones. All arms and propellers must be unfolded before powering on the aircraft, or it may affect Self Diagnostic Testing [1].

rows.question: What action must I take if the 'Critical Low battery level warning' is triggered?
rows.answer: The aircraft must land immediately: allow the aircraft to descend and land automatically [1]. (The aircraft status indicator blinks red quickly, the DJI GO 4 app display flashes red, the aircraft starts to descend and the remote controller sounds an alarm [1].) When the aircraft begins to land automatically, you can push the left stick upward to make the aircraft hover at its current altitude, giving you an opportunity to navigate to a more appropriate landing location [1]. The auto landing cannot be cancelled, but you can use the remote controller to alter the aircraft's orientation during the landing process [2].

rows.question: Describe the 3-step process the aircraft follows when it detects an obstacle during RTH.
rows.reference:
1. Aircraft decelerates when an obstacle is sensed at 49 ft (15 m) ahead.

2. Aircraft stops and hovers then starts ascending vertically to avoid the obstacle. The aircraft will

stop climbing when it is at least 16 ft (5 m) above the detected obstacle.
3. RTH procedures resume.
rows.answer:
Upon detecting an obstacle during RTH (provided lighting conditions are adequate for the Forward Vision System), the aircraft acts as follows [1]:
1. The aircraft decelerates when an obstacle is sensed at 49 ft (15 m) ahead.
2. The aircraft stops and hovers, then starts ascending vertically to avoid the obstacle. It stops climbing when it is at least 16 ft (5 m) above the detected obstacle.
3. RTH procedures resume, and the aircraft continues flying to the Home Point at the current altitude.

rows.question: What types of objects should I specifically AVOID guiding the aircraft towards when using TapFly?
rows.reference: DO NOT guide the aircraft to fly towards people, animals, small and fine objects (e.g. tree\n\nbranches and power lines) or transparent objects (e.g. glass or water).
rows.answer: When using TapFly on the DJI Mavic Pro, DO NOT guide the aircraft to fly towards people, animals, small and fine objects (e.g. tree branches and power lines) or transparent objects (e.g. glass or water). Also watch for obstacles in the flight path and stay clear of them [1].

rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What's the second thing on the pre-flight checklist?
rows.reference: 2. Propellers are mounted correctly and firmly.
rows.answer: The second item on the Preflight Checklist is: "Propellers are mounted correctly and firmly." (The first is that the remote controller, Intelligent Flight Battery, and mobile device are fully charged.) [5]

rows.question: How do I use the QuickShot feature?
rows.reference:
1. Take off and ensure the aircraft is flying at least 4.5 ft (1.5 m) above the ground.
2. Launch DJI GO 4, tap, then select QuickShot, and follow the prompts.
3. Select your target subject in the camera view and choose a shooting mode. Tap “GO” to begin
recording.
rows.answer:
Before starting, ensure that the aircraft is in P Mode and that the Intelligent Flight Battery is charged sufficiently [2]. Then:

1. Take off and ensure the aircraft is flying at least 4.5 ft (1.5 m) above the ground [2].
2. Launch DJI GO 4, tap the icon, then select QuickShot, and follow the prompts [2].
3. Select your target subject in the camera view and choose a shooting mode [2] - Dronie (fly backward and upward, with the camera locked on your subject), Helix (fly upward, spiraling around your subject) or Rocket (ascend with the camera pointing downward) [3].
4. Tap "GO" to begin recording. The aircraft will fly back to its original position after shooting is finished [2].
5. View and edit the generated or original video using Playback [1]; Mavic records a video according to the selected mode and automatically generates a 10-second short video that can be viewed, edited, or shared to social media from the Playback menu [3].

Notes: QuickShot is only available when GPS signal is strong. Tap the icon in DJI GO 4 or pull a control stick opposite to the direction of flight to exit QuickShot anytime during shooting. In QuickShot the aircraft cannot avoid obstacles automatically, so only use it in wide open areas [1].

rows.question: What is the function of the Flight Pause Button?
rows.answer:
On the DJI Mavic Pro, the Flight Pause Button is pressed once for emergency braking [1]. It is also used to exit automated flight modes, after which the aircraft hovers:
- Press it once to exit ActiveTrack, TapFly and Intelligent Navigation flight modes; the aircraft will hover at the current position [5][2][3].
- Press it to exit from RTH; the aircraft will stop ascending and hover [4]. The pilot can also immediately exit Smart RTH with it [6].

rows.question: What does the 'Dronie' QuickShot mode do?
rows.reference: Dronie : Fly backward and upward, with the camera locked on your subject.
rows.answer: Dronie: the aircraft flies backward and upward, with the camera locked on your subject. As a QuickShot mode, the Mavic records a video according to the selected shooting mode and then automatically generates a 10-second short video [1].

rows.question: What does the remote controller error 'STICK ERR' indicate?
rows.reference: Control stick error. Calibrate the control sticks in the DJI GO 4 app.
rows.answer: "STICK ERR" indicates a control stick error. Calibrate the control sticks in the DJI GO 4 app [1]. (The related message "STICK ERR+RE-CTR STCK" means the control stick is not centered and should be re-centered [1].)

rows.question: What are the flight restrictions if the app is not connected or logged in?
rows.reference: flight is restricted to a height of 30 m and distance of 50 m when not connected\nor logged into the app during flight
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What is the minimum braking distance required for S-mode in windless conditions?
rows.reference: A minimum braking distance of 30 meters is required in windless conditions.
rows.answer: A minimum braking distance of 30 meters is required in windless conditions in S-mode (Sport) [1].

rows.question: Identify a type of surface over which the Forward and Downward Vision Systems may not function correctly.
rows.reference: Flying over monochrome surfaces (e.g. pure black, pure white, pure red, pure green).
rows.answer: Water - the Forward and Downward Vision Systems may not function properly when the aircraft is flying over water [2]. Other surfaces the manual lists as problematic include monochrome surfaces (e.g. pure black, pure white, pure red, pure green), highly reflective surfaces, transparent surfaces, moving surfaces or objects [1], inclined surfaces that deflect sound waves away from the aircraft, surfaces that can absorb sound waves (e.g. thick carpet), surfaces without clear patterns or texture, and surfaces with identical repeating patterns or textures (e.g. tiling) [2].

rows.question: What is the safety instruction regarding aged, chipped, or broken propellers?
rows.reference: DO NOT use aged, chipped,\nor broken propellers.
rows.answer: DO NOT use aged, chipped, or broken propellers. Ensure that all propellers are in good condition before each flight [1].

rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: When earthing the Daikin FTXS indoor unit air conditioner, what must the unit never be earthed to?
rows.reference: utility pipe, lightning conductor or telephone earth lead
rows.answer: The unit must never be earthed to a utility pipe, a lightning conductor or a telephone earth lead. Imperfect earthing may result in electric shocks [1].

rows.question: What is the recommended installation height for the Daikin FTXS wall-mounted indoor unit?
rows.answer: The recommended installation height for the Daikin FTXS indoor unit is 1.8m [4].

rows.question: Two Daikin FTXS indoor units are installed in one room and the wireless remote controllers need different addresses. Which jumper do I cut on the indoor unit printed circuit board?
rows.answer: Cut the address jumper (JA) on the indoor unit's printed circuit board, after removing the metal plate electrical wiring cover [1]. (The matching jumper to cut in the remote controller is the address jumper J4 [1].)

rows.question: On the Daikin FTXS indoor unit, which connector does the connection cord attach to when connecting to an HA system such as a wired or central remote controller?
rows.answer: When connecting to an HA system (wired remote controller, central remote controller etc.), the connection cord attaches to the S21 connector [1][2]. Procedure: remove the metal plate electrical wiring cover (refer to the removal/attachment methods of metal plate electrical wiring covers), attach the connection cord to the S21 connector and pull the harness out through the notched part in the figure, then replace the electrical wiring cover as it was and pull the harness around as shown in the figure [1].

rows.question: What diameter feed-through hole should be bored in the wall for the Daikin FTXS indoor unit piping?
rows.answer: Bore a feed-through hole of 65mm in the wall, so that it has a down slope toward the outside [1].

rows.question: How much of the wire ends should be stripped when wiring the terminal block of the Daikin FTXS indoor unit?
rows.answer: On the Daikin FTXS indoor unit, strip the wire ends 15mm [1]. (The 20mm figure in the extracts is from the RXS/RKS outdoor unit manual, not the indoor unit [4].)

rows.question: What nominal diameter of rigid polyvinyl chloride pipe can be joined directly to the drain hose of the Daikin FTXS indoor unit for embedded drain piping?
rows.answer: A rigid polyvinyl chloride pipe of nominal diameter 13mm can be connected directly to the drain hose attached to the indoor unit for embedded piping work, using a commercially available drain socket (nominal diameter 13mm) as a joint [1].

rows.question: On a Daikin FTXS 50 class indoor unit, what flare nut tightening torque applies to the 1/2 inch gas side connection?
rows.answer: For the 50 class (Daikin FTXS indoor unit), the gas side connection is 1/2 inch and the flare nut tightening torque is 49.5-60.3 N·m (505-615 kgf·cm) [1].

rows.question: For a Daikin FTXS 50 class indoor unit, what outside diameter of gas side copper pipe is required?
rows.answer: For the FTXS 50 class indoor unit, the gas side copper pipe must be O.D. 12.7mm (the 20/25/35/42 class uses O.D. 9.5mm) [1]. This corresponds to the 1/2 inch gas side flare size listed for the 50 class [3].

rows.question: During trial operation of a Daikin FTXS indoor unit the symptom is 'remote controller malfunctioning'. According to the test items list, what setting should be checked?
rows.answer: Check that the heat pump or cooling only mode is selectable with the dipswitches of the remote controller (i.e. the heat pump / cooling only dipswitch setting of the remote controller) [1].

rows.question: What is the sound pressure level in dB(A) of the Daikin FTXS35 indoor unit at high fan speed?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: What error code does the Daikin FTXS indoor unit show on the remote controller for a faulty room temperature thermistor?
rows.answer: NOT FOUND

rows.question: Why does the Daikin RXS outdoor unit installation manual say to stop small animals using the outdoor unit as a shelter?
rows.reference: Small animals making contact with electrical parts can cause malfunctions, smoke or fire
rows.answer: Because small animals making contact with electrical parts can cause malfunctions, smoke or fire. The manual says to provide adequate measures to prevent the outdoor unit being used as a shelter by small animals, and to instruct the customer to keep the area around the unit clean [1].

rows.question: How much additional refrigerant must be added to a Daikin RXS outdoor unit for refrigerant pipe exceeding 10m in length?
rows.answer: 20g/m of additional refrigerant is required for refrigerant pipe exceeding 10m in length [1].

rows.question: When a wall stands on the exhaust side of a Daikin RXS outdoor unit, what is the maximum permitted wall height?
rows.answer: The wall height on the exhaust side should be 1200mm or less [1].

rows.question: If the drain port of a Daikin RXS heat pump outdoor unit is covered by the mounting base or floor, how high must the additional foot bases under the unit's feet be?
rows.answer: At least 30mm in height: if the drain port is covered by a mounting base or floor surface, place additional foot bases of at least 30mm in height under the outdoor unit's feet [1].

rows.question: What is the service port cap tightening torque on the Daikin RXS outdoor unit stop valves?
rows.answer: On the Daikin RXS/RKS outdoor unit, the service port cap tightening torque is 10.8-14.7 N·m (110-150 kgf·cm) [1].

rows.question: While vacuuming the lines of a Daikin RXS outdoor unit, the compound pressure gauge pointer swings back after the vacuum pump is stopped. What does that indicate?
rows.reference: refrigerant may have water content or a loose pipe joint may exists
rows.answer: If the compound pressure gauge pointer swings back, the refrigerant may have water content or a loose pipe joint may exist. Check all pipe joints and retighten nuts as needed, then repeat steps 2) through 4) [1].

rows.question: What GWP value is listed for the refrigerant used in the Daikin RXS outdoor unit?
rows.answer: The GWP (global warming potential) value listed is 1975, for refrigerant type R410A [1].

rows.question: On the Daikin RXS outdoor unit, what do I disconnect to turn ON the standby electricity saving function?
rows.reference: the selective connector for standby electricity saving
rows.answer:
Disconnect the selective connector for standby electricity saving [1]. Procedure for turning ON the standby electricity saving function [1]:
1. Check that the main power supply is turned OFF. Turn it OFF if it has not been turned OFF.
2. Remove the stop valve cover.
3. Disconnect the selective connector for standby electricity saving.
4. Turn ON the main power supply.
Before connecting or disconnecting the selective connector, make sure that the main power supply is turned OFF. The function is turned OFF before shipping, and the selective connector is required if an indoor unit other than the applicable ones is connected [1]. The function works only on indoor units FTXS20G2V1B, FTXS25G2V1B, FTXS35G2V1B, ATXS20G2V1B, ATXS25G2V1B and ATXS35G2V1B [2].

rows.question: Which jumper on the Daikin RXS outdoor unit circuit board is cut for the facility setting that extends cooling operation down to -15°C outdoor temperature?
rows.answer: Jumper 8 (J8) on the circuit board. Cutting it expands the operation range down to -15°C; however, the unit will stop if the outdoor temperature drops below -20°C and start back up once the temperature rises again [1]. Cutting J8 also sets the indoor fan tap to the highest position, and the user should be notified of this [5]. This function is only for facilities (where the target of air conditioning is equipment such as computers) and must never be used in a residence or office [1].

rows.question: What contact point gap is required for the all-pole disconnection breaker used on the Daikin RXS outdoor unit power supply?
rows.answer: Use an all-pole disconnection type breaker with at least 3mm between the contact point gaps [1].

rows.answer: NOT FOUND
